question.text: Comparing option exercise styles across derivative markets in India: which is correct?

answer.text: All exchange-traded options in India are European-style — equity (index and stock), currency, and commodity options can only be exercised at expiry
Equity options are American; currency options are European; commodity options vary
All options in India are American-style allowing exercise at any time
Index options are European; all others are American-style

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series VIII pages 61 and 63 confirm that exchange-traded index and stock options in India are European-style and that exercise/assignment occur only on the expiration date. Series I page 90 states that currency options in India are also European-only, and Series XVI page 66 says the same about commodity options under current norms. The Trap: Equity options are not American in India, the universal "American" claim is incorrect, and the European style is not restricted to index options — it applies uniformly to listed equity, currency and commodity options. Note: Pricing-model implications (e.g. Black-Scholes) and dividend-capture early-exercise behaviour are not covered in the pages checked, so the explanation stays with the supported European-style statement only.
